rules.summary: Generation inputs match explicit manifest selections.
Current reference content matches the recorded hash.
Ordered roles and prompt bindings agree.
Control-only references stay outside generation requests.
Unknown or existing submissions reconcile rather than resubmit.
Selected parameters and reference mode have current capability evidence.
Narrative action has an observable event and end state.

A narrative, ad, micro-drama, music-video or showcase shot carries a recorded shot plan with duration, size, angle, camera move, lens intent and a named light source with its key side, or a recorded static reason.
exceptions: User lock, static-by-design format (the `ugc`, `ugc-how-to`, `ugc-unboxing`, `product-review` and `ugc-virtual-try-on` modes, named UGC presets with a locked camera block, talking-head, avatar and news takes, frame-break), explicit per-shot camera plan from another skill (a pin plan; a music-video genre lock is vocabulary, not an exemption), plate for cutdown, source-preserving edit, extension continuation, or no video shot record the exemption instead.

rules.summary: Adjacent shots in a cutting clip differ in at least two of size family, angle class, camera move and key side; each scene has a non-eye-level angle, a motivated move at its energy level and uneven shot lengths, or a recorded reason.
exceptions: A single continuous take records its camera path and light progression instead of neighbor contrast.
A shot plan derived from another skill's camera plan treats these checks as advisory.

rules.summary: A confirmed project camera, lens, lighting, pacing or energy axis recorded in directorial_axes or the locked block appears in the shot prompt, or the scene records an override with its reason.
Visible design follows approved or requested descriptors.
Exact static copy and geometry use the deterministic graphics route rather than generative image synthesis.
A deterministic raster has a schema-valid render record bound to its source, inputs, renderer, copy, dimensions, alpha intent, and output hash.
A transparent delivery asset contains real alpha and is distinct from any solid-background model reference.
Changes stay within may_change and preserve declared locks.
All applicable checks have complete request-bound evidence.
The production canvas declares the stage being completed and exposes its required evidence.
The generated HTML matches the current canvas manifest and all referenced local sources.
Template analysis contains the complete structured breakdown required by downstream stages.
Shot indices and timing form one finite, ordered, continuous source timeline.
Element identifiers are unique and their shot and keyframe references resolve.
Motion evidence is bound to the exact approved breakdown bytes.
Motion evidence covers each approved shot exactly once without changing its boundaries.
Motion observations, confidence, uncertainty, and directing language are complete.
An object swap identifies the original by observable descriptors and fully replaces it in every frame with only the target visible.
An object swap states the target count and inherits every appearance, motion, occlusion, exit, and timing of the original.
A recast motion source supplies motion, camera, framing, cuts, and timing only; appearance comes from the bound references.
Every visible source subject is mapped, removed, or kept as a background extra, with no unresolved ambiguity.
Each mapped subject is identified by observable descriptors and bound to exactly one reference.
A recast states per-cut person counts and keeps source accessories and extra people out of the rebuilt cast.
A recast states one audio route and lip-sync expectations that agree with it.
A video-to-video request binds the recorded muted source master with generate_audio false and adds sound in post.
exceptions: A recorded, user-requested native-audio exception for a named take.

rules.summary: Every person or character identity reference is a Virtual Portrait asset registered from an approved invented design.
A restyle keeps the source subjects, layout, actions, camera, cuts and timing and changes only the rendering medium.
A restyle style reference supplies only medium, palette, line, texture and light quality, never subjects or layout.
